findings.location: stopped_observation, lines 229 through 234; decode_inventory, lines 142 and 198; DockerLocalCommands.containers, line 370
findings.title: Valid multiwriter observations fail reconciliation when enrollment order differs from CID order
findings.reproduction: Static counterexample, not an executed additional probe: enroll two otherwise valid writers in manifest order [b repeated 64 times, a repeated 64 times], with their matching process/configuration entries and both observed cleanly stopped. Supply identical before/after Docker inventories in sorted CID order, as DockerLocalCommands.containers constructs them. decode_inventory accepts the exact set and returns writers in [a, b] order. stopped_observation compares that list positionally against [b, a] and raises 'Every original writer must be observed stopped before capture'.
findings.evidence: validate_manifest in lab/storage_write_settlement.py lines 169 through 184 allows unique writers in any order. DockerLocalCommands.containers at line 370 passes sorted(ids) to inspect. decode_inventory iterates containers_before at line 142 and appends each writer at line 198 without restoring manifest order. stopped_observation at lines 229 through 234 uses zip with the manifest list and requires positional CID equality. LocalNativeAuthority.reconcile at line 683 and DockerLocalCommands.storage_rows at line 460 invoke this validator, so a valid enrolled multiwriter set can stop successfully yet cannot perform file/row capture. The approved 142 Python, 3 hybrid and 78 Bun checks all pass; native authority tests construct a one-writer candidate and do not cover the reversed two-writer parser composition. No native admission bypass or actual service failure is claimed.
findings.requested_change: Normalize decoded writer observations to the manifest order, or validate the complete unique stopped set by CID while preserving exact identity checks. Add a private source regression that composes decode_inventory with stopped_observation for a reverse-ordered two-writer manifest and sorted Docker observations, retaining missing/duplicate/foreign/running-writer refusals.
